name: Locking
notes: Locking style pack (Doc 04 template). The dance Don Campbell created by accident in 1970 Los Angeles — a freeze mid-Funky-Chicken that the crowd laughed at, a point back at the crowd, and a vocabulary was born ('Campbellocking'). Codified with The Lockers (1973): Toni Basil, Fred 'Rerun' Berry, Jimmy 'Scoo B Doo' Foster, Greg 'Campbellock Jr.' Pope and crew, broadcast to the world on Soul Train. Design truths: locking rides UP on the beat where hip hop bounces down; showmanship, character and HUMOR are core technique, not garnish — the pack grades your face as much as your lock. Named moves keep their creators' names. No knee drops or splits in v1 — they wait for readiness gates and in-person coaching.

seasons.finale: Film 8 counts: loose funk groove slammed into clean locks — fast, FROZEN, released on beat.
Film a point-and-twirl combination on beat — eyes following every point, attitude on.
Film Scoo B Doos chained with Stop 'n Go — kicks lifted, paddles clean, locks dead-stopped.
Film Which-a-Ways and Funky Guitar WITH your face in it — play, mug, perform. Stone faces fail this one.
Perform for actual humans: a party line, a cypher round, or a filmed show with a costume touch — stripes, hat, anything that says The Lockers walked here.

attributes.name: Wrist twirl control L1
attributes.test: 20 clean wrist twirls each hand, elbows held high and quiet, no shoulder creep

attributes.name: Full-out stamina L1
attributes.test: one full funk song of high-energy grooving — locking has no half-power setting

attributes.name: Shoulder freedom L1
attributes.test: 20 big loose backward arm swings each side, shoulders never hiking to the ears

nodes.name: Funk and the ONE
checkpoints: locking is funk's dance: James Brown, Sly Stone, early 70s grooves
find the ONE — locks and points land on the accents
locking rides UP on the beat: chest lifts where hip hop drops

nodes.name: Dancing the stops — silence is a beat
checkpoints: a lock held through a horn stab reads louder than any move
speed means nothing without the freeze that frames it

nodes.name: Don Campbell and the accidental lock (1970, Los Angeles)
checkpoints: Don Campbell froze mid-Funky-Chicken because he forgot the next step — the crowd laughed, and he kept the freeze: the Lock
he pointed back at the people laughing — the Point became vocabulary
the dance carried his name first: Campbellocking
lesson under the lore: your 'mistake' can be your signature if you own it

nodes.name: The Lockers and Soul Train
checkpoints: The Lockers (1973): Don Campbell, Toni Basil, Fred 'Rerun' Berry, Jimmy 'Scoo B Doo' Foster, Greg 'Campbellock Jr.' Pope and crew
Soul Train carried locking into every living room in America
they dressed the part — stripes, knickers, big hats, big socks: costume is part of the tradition

nodes.name: Showmanship: humor is technique
checkpoints: locking is generous — it plays TO the audience, mugs, jokes, gives
a technically perfect round with a dead face is an unfinished round
watch Lockers-era footage: count how often they smile

nodes.name: The up groove
checkpoints: chest lifts ON the beat — the groove goes up
arms swing big and loose; locking hates small
knees soft, energy forward, ready to explode
mistakes: bouncing down like a hip hop groove

nodes.name: The Lock
nodes.origin: Don Campbell, 1970 — the accidental freeze that named the dance
nodes.anchor: learnable today; the SNAP takes months
checkpoints: from full-speed motion, slam to a dead stop in a slight crouch — forearms up, body braced
the lock is a pose with muscle behind it, held for a beat
contrast is everything: the faster the before, the harder the lock reads
release back into groove like nothing happened
mistakes: a soft stop with no snap
locking so long the groove dies
collapsing the chest in the crouch

nodes.name: The Point
nodes.origin: Don Campbell — he pointed at the crowd laughing at him, and it became vocabulary
checkpoints: full arm extension at shoulder height, index finger loaded with intent
eyes go WHERE the point goes — you and the audience look together
hold it a beat; a point is a sentence, not a twitch
mistakes: eyes elsewhere — an unwatched point says nothing

nodes.name: Wrist twirls
checkpoints: elbows high, forearms roll — the twirl is round and lazy-looking but exact
twirl INTO locks and points; it's the connective tissue
both hands equal — the weak hand gets double reps

nodes.name: Pacing
checkpoints: palm punches forward in rhythm — half-beat jabs that set up the big accent
pacing is a drumroll; the lock or point is the cymbal

nodes.name: Scoo B Doo
nodes.origin: created by Jimmy 'Scoo B Doo' Foster of The Lockers — say his name when you do it
checkpoints: kick-step with a lean-back, arms paddling in time
the kick lifts light and sharp; the lean has swagger, not fall
finish locked — every Scoo B Doo lands somewhere

nodes.name: Stop 'n Go
nodes.origin: Lockers-era vocabulary — the step that walks in and rewinds out
checkpoints: step in, lock — then reverse out the exact door you entered
the rewind sells it: same path, same timing, backwards
lock dead-still between directions
mistakes: exiting a different way than you entered
no true stop between the stop and the go

nodes.name: Which-a-Way
checkpoints: leg swings side to side while the body asks 'which way?' — indecision as choreography
locks punctuate each fake-out
play it to someone; the joke needs a receiver

nodes.name: Funky Guitar
checkpoints: lean back and strum an invisible guitar in rhythm
it's a bit — commit to the bit
twirl out of it into a point for the button

nodes.name: The 8×8 routine — filmed with character
checkpoints: eight 8-counts chaining groove, locks, points, twirls, Scoo B Doo, Stop 'n Go
every accent in the music gets acknowledged
your face performs the whole 64 counts

nodes.name: Showtime — perform for humans
checkpoints: a party line, a cypher round, or a show for friends — witnessed, not just filmed
one costume touch in honor of The Lockers
make one person laugh mid-round; that's the tradition working
